title: Run
description: One execution of one benchmark binary, written whether it succeeded or failed. A Run describes itself: it holds the parameters the binary was given, the provider's own words for where it ran, the bytes that ran, the box's environment before and after, and the binary's stdout, whose lines are its events. Nothing in it is a judgement. Every value of the form sha256:<hex> names a blob stored at blobs/sha256/<hex> whose bytes hash to it. The root is closed: a key not listed here makes a record invalid.

oneOf.description: The older shape: written before the runner stopped copying stdout into the Run, it carries the events.
The shape written since: the stdout blob's size and lines, and no copy of its events.

schema.description: What this file is, and which version of its shape.

id.description: A version 7 UUID, minted on the box when the binary is launched.

boot.description: The kernel's boot id. The Runs of one boot share it.

started_at.description: Read just before the binary was launched.

ended_at.description: Read just after the binary exited.

benchmark.description: The benchmark's name, as the schedule entry gives it. The binary was built from the directory of that name under benchmarks in the source archive (source), a git archive of source_commit.

params.description: Exactly the parameters delivered to the binary, as LM_PARAM_<KEY>.

additionalProperties.description: One parameter's value, under its key: delivered to the binary as LM_PARAM_<KEY>, the key upper-cased, a boolean as true or false.

samples.description: Delivered to the binary as LM_SAMPLES.

service.description: Present when the schedule entry named a Service the benchmark measures, such as s3_fixtures (the stage's private bucket of Fixtures). Its inputs were delivered to the binary beside its params, each as LM_SERVICE_<KEY>. `inputs` holds every input that is not secret, exactly as delivered; `secret_inputs` names the ones that are, such as short-lived keys, whose values are never written anywhere: not here, not in a blob, a dump, the boot summary or a log.

name.description: The Service, as the schedule entry names it.

inputs.description: Every input of the Service that is not secret, by name, exactly as delivered to the binary as LM_SERVICE_<KEY>: for s3_fixtures, endpoint and region.

additionalProperties.description: One input's value, exactly as delivered.

secret_inputs.description: The names of the Service's secret inputs, delivered to the binary as LM_SERVICE_<KEY>, whose values are written nowhere: for s3_fixtures, aws_access_key_id, aws_secret_access_key and aws_session_token.

source_commit.description: The git commit the source archive was made from.

source.description: The source archive the box unpacked and built from.

binary.description: The binary that ran, as the box built it: its bytes, the build, the compiler, what the build printed, and what the compiler resolved its flags to.

build.description: The name of the build, as given to the benchmark's Makefile.

compiler.description: The compiler's own first line of version output.

command.description: What the build printed: the commands it ran.

resolved_flags.description: What the compiler resolved its flags to on this box, such as -march=native.

provider.description: Where this ran, in the provider's own words: under LedgerMath's names for them, each value is the provider's, verbatim, or null when the box could not read it. `name` says whose words the values are.

name.description: Whose words the other keys' values are: aws; or unknown, with no other key, when the box could not read its instance ID from the instance metadata service.

additionalProperties.description: One fact of where the binary ran: the key is LedgerMath's name for it, the value the provider's words, verbatim; null when the box could not read that value. For aws, read from the instance metadata service: instance_type, region, availability_zone, availability_zone_id, image_id (the service's ami-id) and instance_id.

environment.description: The box's environment dump taken just before the launch and just after the exit. Each names an index blob that lists the dump's sections by hash.

before.description: The index blob of the dump taken just before the binary was launched.

after.description: The index blob of the dump taken just after the binary exited.

runner.description: The runner that launched the binary: a blob listing every file of the directory named runner in the source archive (source), one line each, its sha256 in hex, two spaces and its path within that directory, sorted by path, leaving out any directory named build or __pycache__.

exit.description: How the process ended: its exit code, or the signal that killed it. `timeout_seconds` is present when the runner killed it for running that long. `runner_signal` is present when the runner was told to stop before it collected the binary's exit: see $defs/runner_signal.

code.description: The binary's exit status, when it exited by itself rather than being killed by a signal. 0 means it completed. Any other code means what the benchmark says it means, and does not by itself mean the binary stopped short: http_get exits 4 after finishing its stream when a request failed (a status that is not 2xx among them), a kept connection could not be set up, or the Run ended early; and a binary exits 2 after printing started alone when it cannot run its parameter set. Method series v1 counts a Run only when its code is 0; Method requests v1 accepts 4 as well.

signal.description: The number of the signal that ended the binary.

timeout_seconds.description: The runner's timeout for the execution, in seconds: present only when the runner killed the binary (signal 9) for running that long.

events.description: Carried only by Runs written before the runner stopped copying stdout into the Run (they have no `stdout_bytes`): every line the binary printed to stdout, parsed, in order, stopping at the first line that is not a JSON object. Later Runs do not carry it. For every Run the `stdout` blob is the source of its events (one per line, each of the shape the events schema gives, which the data API serves at v1/schemas/events.schema.json), and every reader reads them there; for a Run that carries `events`, they must equal the blob's lines.

t.description: Whole nanoseconds on the clock that the stream's started event names.

events_error.description: Carried, like `events`, only by Runs written before the runner stopped copying stdout into the Run, when a stdout line could not be parsed: the line's number and why. A reader of a later Run finds such a line when it parses the `stdout` blob.

line.description: The number of the stdout line that could not be parsed, counting from 1.

message.description: Why it could not be parsed: not JSON, with the parser's error, or not a JSON object.

stdout.description: The binary's stdout, verbatim: one event per line, each of the shape the events schema gives, which the data API serves at v1/schemas/events.schema.json. The source of the Run's events for every Run.

stdout_bytes.description: The length of the stdout blob, in bytes. Written, with `stdout_lines`, by every Run since the runner stopped copying stdout into the Run; such a Run carries no `events`.

stdout_lines.description: The number of lines in the stdout blob: the pieces between newlines, a last line without one counted too. Written with `stdout_bytes`.

runner_signal.description: The signal that told the runner to stop (15 SIGTERM, 2 SIGINT, 1 SIGHUP), received after the runner launched the binary and before it collected the binary's exit. The runner then killed the binary if it had not ended, and started no further execution. `code` or `signal` beside it is still how the binary actually ended. A stop signal that arrives after the exit was collected stops the boot but is not recorded here.
